chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «So do not perform self-righteousness of yourselves. He is more knowledgeable of who is the godfearing.»
He said: It is (like) the saying of a person: «I prayed yesterday» and «I fasted yesterday» and the like of this.

Then he, peace be upon him, said: Indeed, a people used to wake up and say: «We prayed yesterday», and: «We fasted yesterday», to which Ali, peace be upon him, said: However, I, indeed, sleep at night and day, and if I was to find anything (of free time) between them, I would have slept during it.

key_terms.فَلَا تُزَكُّوا أَنفُسَكُمْ: So do not perform self-righteousness of yourselves
key_terms.هُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَنِ اتَّقَى: He is more knowledgeable of who is the godfearing

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'do not perform self-righteousness' in Surah An-Najm according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration to define the specific form of *nafs* (self) praised in Surah An-Najm as boasting about acts of worship, a subtle vice where one seeks validation for piety. The Imam’s contrast with Imam Ali highlights the distinction between mere ritual performance and the profound humility of the truly devout, who are too absorbed in devotion to count their deeds. This interpretation aligns with Shia exegetical tradition that views self-praise as a corruption of sincerity (*ikhlas*).

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, from Ya’qoub bin Yazid, from Muhammed bin Abi ‘Umayr, from Jameel bin Darraj, that he said: I asked Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him,
about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: «So do not perform self-righteousness of yourselves. He is more knowledgeable of who is the godfearing.» [53:32]
He said: It is (like) the saying of a person: «I prayed yesterday» and «I fasted yesterday» and the like of this.

Then he, peace be upon him, said: Indeed, a people used to wake up and say: «We prayed yesterday», and: «We fasted yesterday», to which Ali, peace be upon him, said: However, I, indeed, sleep at night and day, and if I was to find anything (of free time) between them, I would have slept during it.
